metadata.agent_last_message:
I've built the `iges` tool in `output/`, with entry point `output/main.js`. All five subcommands (`parse`, `write`, `query`, `eval`, `roundtrip`) work on my test files. It uses only the Node standard library and has no `package.json`.

**What I tested.** The workspace had no sample IGES files, so I tested on files I made myself:
- **Round-trip:** every one of the 87 entity types survives write → parse → write with byte-identical output. A second `roundtrip` pass over its own output is also byte-identical, as your spec requires.
- **Hand-written "real-world style" file:** it has CRLF line endings, `D` exponents (`1.0D1`), a 2-digit-year timestamp, defaulted fields, text after the record delimiter, and extra trailing pointers. It parses and round-trips correctly.
- **Rejections:** each of these exits 1 with the field name, spec section, line number and section in the diagnostic:
  - a negative entity type
  - a zero `param_line_count`
  - bad `view`/`xform_matrix` pointers
  - a zero-length Line
  - non-positive Global fields
  - a missing Terminate section
  - a prohibited delimiter
  - control characters in a Start line or a Hollerith string
  - an even or missing `query --de`
  - malformed JSON on `write` (no `.iges` file is left behind)
- **Evaluation:** I checked arcs (with a transformation matrix), lines, B-spline curves and surfaces, composite curves, conics, surfaces of revolution, tabulated cylinders, cylindrical surfaces and offset surfaces against values worked out by hand. There is no reference implementation here to compare against, so the 1e-9 tolerance hasn't been checked.

**Where I had to guess.** Your spec was ambiguous on these points, so results may differ from the reference implementation:
- **Offset curve (130):** I normalise `(vx, vy, vz)` to unit length before adding `d1` times it. If your vectors are already unit length, this makes no difference.
- **Analytic surfaces without a reference direction (form 0):** the tool uses the global X axis, o
